definition.name: The Awakening
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Truth vs. a comfortable lie — Is it better to know an unbearable reality or to live a pleasant illusion?
definition.summary: Neo is drawn from his mundane, compliant existence by an unseen guide who offers him a choice between forgetting and knowing, leading him to swallow the red pill. This decision forces him to confront the horrifying truth that his world is a simulation and humanity is farmed for power, causing him to recoil from the violation. He ultimately accepts this harsh reality, rejecting the comfortable ignorance represented by Cypher’s desire to return to the lie.

chain.why_in_plot: This event initiates the plot's core dilemma by presenting Neo with the choice between his mundane existence and the unknown truth. It establishes the 'unseen guide' and the initial pull away from compliance.
chain.caused_by_previous: The plot's throughline begins here. Neo's dissatisfaction with his 'mundane, compliant existence' (established in the summary) is the precondition that makes him receptive to the contact and the 'white rabbit' instruction.

chain.why_in_plot: This event reinforces the 'comfortable lie' side of the dilemma. Neo's return to his job and his deferential compliance with Rhineheart demonstrate the safety and predictability of the illusion he is about to leave.
chain.caused_by_previous: The night's events in ev-004 collapse into the next morning, showing the immediate reassertion of the status quo. The contrast between the mysterious contact and the boring office life heightens the stakes of the upcoming choice.

chain.why_in_plot: The threat of the Agents forces Neo to choose between staying in the lie (and being arrested/killed) or accepting the help of the 'unseen guide' (Morpheus/Trinity). It breaks the safety of the illusion.
chain.caused_by_previous: The contact in ev-004 and the subsequent attention drawn by Neo's actions lead to the Agents closing in. The warning from Morpheus in ev-006 is the direct consequence of Neo being 'summoned' and identified in ev-004.

chain.why_in_plot: The interrogation represents the system's attempt to enforce the lie. Agent Smith offers a deal to wipe Neo's record (return to comfort/ignorance) in exchange for betraying the truth (Morpheus). Neo's refusal marks his rejection of the comfortable lie.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo is captured because he failed to escape in ev-006. The Agents' presence is the direct result of the manhunt initiated in ev-006.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo is rescued from the Agents' control. This event transitions him from the world of the lie to the threshold of the truth. He accepts the 'Yes' to Morpheus, committing to the path of knowing.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's refusal in ev-007 and the subsequent implantation leave him vulnerable. The rescue by Morpheus's crew is enabled by the prior contact and Neo's implicit choice to side with them over the Agents.

chain.why_in_plot: The removal of the bug is the physical severing of Neo's connection to the surveillance state of the Matrix. It is a necessary step before he can fully enter the real world.
chain.caused_by_previous: The bug was implanted in ev-007. Neo must be 'cleaned' by Trinity in ev-009 before he can safely proceed to the final choice in ev-010.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the pivotal moment of the plot: the choice between the blue pill (forgetting/comfortable lie) and the red pill (knowing/unbearable reality). Neo swallows the red pill, explicitly choosing truth over illusion.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo is brought to Morpheus in ev-008/009. Morpheus frames the choice in ev-010, directly addressing the theme of 'Truth vs. a comfortable lie.' Neo's prior rejection of the Agents' offer in ev-007 predisposes him to this choice.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo confronts the 'horrifying truth' that his world is a simulation and humanity is farmed. This fulfills the 'unbearable reality' part of the theme. He recoils from the violation, experiencing the shock of truth.
chain.caused_by_previous: Swallowing the red pill in ev-010 triggers the extraction process. The physical birth into the real world in ev-011 is the direct mechanical consequence of the choice made in ev-010.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo begins to process the reality. Morpheus starts dismantling his assumptions, moving Neo from shock to understanding. This is the beginning of accepting the harsh reality.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo is recovered from the birth process in ev-011. His physical rebuilding in ev-012 is necessary for him to be conscious enough to receive Morpheus's teachings.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus reveals the full extent of the truth (the desert of the real). Neo's resistance and eventual acceptance of the violation solidify his stance: he chooses the truth, even though it is painful and violates his previous existence.
chain.caused_by_previous: The physical recovery in ev-012 allows Neo to be jacked into the Construct. Morpheus's explanation in ev-013 is the intellectual counterpart to the physical shock of ev-011.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo accepts that there is 'no going back.' This marks the completion of his transition from the comfortable lie to the harsh reality. He commits to the path of the truth.
chain.caused_by_previous: The revelation in ev-013 leads to Neo's acceptance in ev-014. The prophecy discussion reinforces that his choice was fated/destined, helping him reconcile with the loss of his old life.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher represents the counter-argument: the desire to return to the comfortable lie. His disillusionment and deal with Smith highlight the theme by showing what Neo has rejected. It contrasts Neo's acceptance with Cypher's rejection.
chain.caused_by_previous: The training and revelations (ev-015-019) create the environment where Cypher's resentment grows. Cypher's conversation with Neo in ev-020 is enabled by Neo's presence on the ship and the shared knowledge of the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher's betrayal is the violent manifestation of the 'comfortable lie' option. He kills the crew to return to the Matrix. Neo's survival and Tank's intervention represent the triumph of the truth-seekers over those who would choose the illusion.
chain.caused_by_previous: Cypher's deal in ev-020 sets up the betrayal. The crew's return to the ship in ev-028 allows Cypher to execute his plan in ev-029.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo chooses to rescue Morpheus, not because of prophecy, but because of belief in the man and the mission. This is a reaffirmation of his choice of truth and loyalty over self-preservation or comfortable detachment.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's capture in ev-025/026 and the crew's regrouping in ev-027/030 lead to Neo's decision in ev-032. Neo's denial of being the One shows he acts on personal conviction, not just destiny.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo stands and fights Smith, rejecting the option to run (which would be a form of evasion). He accepts the confrontation with the system (the lie/enforcers) head-on.
chain.caused_by_previous: The escape in ev-036/037 leaves Neo trapped. His decision to turn and face Smith in ev-038 is a direct response to being cornered, choosing truth/confrontation over flight.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's death and resurrection, triggered by Trinity's love and belief, symbolizes the ultimate acceptance of the truth. He dies to the old world and is reborn into the new understanding, fully integrated with the reality of the Matrix.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's fight in ev-039 leads to his apparent death in ev-043. Trinity's kiss and Neo's awakening in ev-044 are the culmination of his journey, confirming his status as 'The One' who has mastered the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo awakens to the code of the Matrix. He no longer sees the illusion as real but as manipulable code. This is the final state of 'knowing'—he has transcended the lie and can now control it.
chain.caused_by_previous: The resurrection in ev-044 grants Neo this new perspective. His ability to stop the bullets and destroy Smith in ev-045 is the direct result of his awakening to the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo flies, declaring his freedom. He has fully accepted the harsh reality and now wields power within it. The plot concludes with him rejecting the constraints of the simulation entirely.
chain.caused_by_previous: The destruction of Smith in ev-045 and the escape in ev-046 allow Neo to return to the Matrix with his new powers. His flight in ev-047 is the final assertion of his choice of truth over the comfortable lie.

definition.name: The Identity Crisis
definition.summary: Neo is repeatedly labeled 'the One' by Morpheus and the Oracle, creating a tension between external destiny and internal self-conception. He actively rejects this title, denying he is the One even as he commits to dangerous actions, insisting his choices are wagers on faith rather than prophecy. It is only after his death and revival that he seizes the identity, halting bullets and reading the Matrix as code, resolving the split between Thomas Anderson and Neo.

chain.why_in_plot: Establishes the initial external labeling of Neo as 'the One' by an unseen force (Trinity/Morpheus), setting up the tension between his ordinary self (Thomas Anderson) and the prophesied identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Sets the chain moving: The mysterious summons introduces the concept of Neo's hidden significance, triggering his internal conflict and curiosity.

chain.why_in_plot: Contrasts the external destiny with Neo's internal desire for normalcy. His compliance with Rhineheart shows his current self-conception as a subordinate, ordinary man, resisting the 'hero' narrative.
chain.caused_by_previous: The night's supernatural pull (ev-004) collapses into the mundane reality of his day job, highlighting the split between his two lives.

chain.why_in_plot: The external world forces the issue. Neo is physically hunted because of who he is suspected to be. His hesitation on the ledge represents his internal refusal to accept the 'One' role; he cannot yet make the leap of faith required by the prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: His association with the mysterious group (ev-004) and his failure to fully commit to his ordinary life (ev-005) leads to the Agents closing in, forcing a choice he is not ready to make.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo explicitly rejects the external identity imposed by the Agents (who view him as a criminal/asset) and refuses to betray Morpheus. He asserts his own agency, even in captivity, denying the 'One' label's utility to his captors.
chain.caused_by_previous: Captured by the Agents (ev-006), he is interrogated. His refusal to cooperate is an assertion of his self-conception over the external pressure to conform to the system's view of him.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus explicitly names Neo 'the One' and demands a 'Yes.' Neo's physical state (mouthless) mirrors his inability to verbally claim this identity yet. He is being reclaimed by the prophecy, but remains passive.
chain.caused_by_previous: The Agents' violation (ev-007) leaves him vulnerable, allowing Morpheus's crew to extract him. The 'Yes' demanded is the first direct confrontation with the identity crisis.

chain.why_in_plot: The choice of the Red Pill is the first active step toward accepting a new identity, but it is framed as a choice to know the truth, not necessarily to become the One. It initiates the dismantling of Thomas Anderson's self-conception.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having been extracted (ev-008) and cleaned (ev-009), Neo faces the binary choice. He chooses the path that destroys his old identity, though he does not yet embrace the new one fully.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus begins 'dismantling his assumptions about himself.' This is the systematic deconstruction of Thomas Anderson's identity to make room for Neo's, directly addressing 'Who am I, really?'
chain.caused_by_previous: The physical rebirth (ev-011) necessitates a psychological rebuilding. Morpheus takes charge of this identity reconstruction.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's resistance to the truth of the Matrix is a resistance to his new reality. His physical rejection (vomiting) symbolizes the psychological rejection of the identity that comes with this knowledge.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's dismantling of assumptions (ev-012) culminates in the revelation of the Matrix's true nature, which Neo's mind struggles to integrate.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus explicitly recounts the prophecy and declares 'the search is over,' directly imposing the 'One' identity on Neo. Neo's acceptance that 'there is no going back' is the first step in accepting the weight of this identity, even if he doesn't yet believe he is the One.
chain.caused_by_previous: The trauma of the revelation (ev-013) leaves Neo vulnerable and isolated, making him receptive to Morpheus's narrative of destiny.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's failure in the dojo proves he is not yet the One. His belief that he 'knows kung fu' is a superficial identity; Morpheus's physical defeat of him shatters this false self-conception, forcing him to confront his inadequacy.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's commitment to training (ev-014) leads to the physical tests that reveal the gap between Neo's self-image and the reality of the prophecy.

chain.why_in_plot: The jump failure is a direct test of faith. Neo's inability to jump is his inability to believe in his own power/identity. The crew's division reflects the external pressure to believe in him, which he cannot yet meet.
chain.caused_by_previous: The sparring failure (ev-015) shifts the focus from physical skill to mental belief, leading to the jump test.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher explicitly challenges the 'One' narrative, calling it a 'body count' and a lie. This introduces the counter-argument to Neo's identity crisis: that the prophecy is a tool of manipulation, not destiny. Neo is 'shaken rather than converted,' showing his uncertainty.
chain.caused_by_previous: The repeated failures in training (ev-015, ev-016) make Neo vulnerable to Cypher's cynicism, which attacks the validity of the identity he is being forced to accept.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo meets the Oracle, the source of the prophecy. His hesitation at the door shows his fear of the answer. The Oracle's role is to define his identity, and he is terrified of what she will say.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's insistence on the Oracle's importance (ev-014) and Neo's growing doubt (ev-020) drive him to seek the definitive answer about his identity.

chain.why_in_plot: The Oracle tells Neo he is NOT the One, but that he will have to choose between his life and Morpheus's. This is the peak of the identity crisis: he is explicitly denied the 'One' label, forcing him to define himself by his choices, not his destiny.
chain.caused_by_previous: Entering the Oracle's domain (ev-022) leads to the direct confrontation with the prophecy's verdict.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus sacrifices himself, believing Neo is the One. Neo's survival is due to Morpheus's faith, not Neo's own power. This deepens the crisis: he is saved by a prophecy he has been told is false, creating a paradox.
chain.caused_by_previous: The trap springs (ev-023), and Morpheus acts on his belief in Neo's identity, sacrificing himself to save the 'One'.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo explicitly denies being the One ('I'm not the One') but chooses to rescue Morpheus anyway. This is the core resolution of the 'internal self-conception' part of the theme: he acts on faith and love, not because he believes he is the One, but because he chooses to be the person who saves his savi
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's capture (ev-025) and the Oracle's denial (ev-023) leave Neo with a choice: accept the false prophecy or act on his own moral compass. He chooses the latter.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo stands to fight Smith, not because he believes he is the One, but because he has decided to face his fate. Morpheus sees 'belief' in Neo's stillness, but Neo is still operating on choice, not prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: The successful rescue (ev-034) leads to the final confrontation. Neo's decision to stand is the culmination of his choice to act, regardless of his identity.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces. He summons power not because he is the One, but because he refuses to die. This is the breaking point of the old identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Facing Smith (ev-038), Neo is pushed to the edge of death, forcing a reaction that transcends his previous limitations.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's death and revival are the catalyst for the final identity shift. Trinity's belief (love) and Neo's choice to return (faith) merge. The 'miracle' is not just power, but the acceptance of a new self.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's refusal to die (ev-039) leads to his death in the Matrix (ev-043), which triggers the real-world crisis and Trinity's intervention.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo seizes the identity. He halts bullets and reads code, resolving the split between Thomas Anderson and Neo. He no longer denies the title; he embodies the power that defines it. The identity crisis is resolved by acceptance and action.
chain.caused_by_previous: The revival (ev-044) unlocks his potential, allowing him to finally accept and use the power associated with 'the One'.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo flies, fully embracing his new identity. He is no longer running or denying; he is in control. The theme 'Who am I, really?' is answered: he is the One, not because of prophecy, but because he chose to be.
chain.caused_by_previous: Awakening to his power (ev-045) and escaping the immediate threat (ev-046) leads to his final assertion of self.

definition.name: The Rescue
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: After Morpheus sacrifices himself to save Neo from capture, the crew faces the dilemma of escaping to preserve their own lives or returning to a certain death to save Morpheus. Neo chooses the path of sacrifice, admitting he is not the One and thus making the mission a gamble on a man rather than a guarantee of destiny. This choice drives the assault on the government building, where Neo’s willingness to risk everything ultimately leads to his own death and subsequent resurrection.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the inciting incident of the specific dilemma: Morpheus's self-sacrifice to save Neo creates the debt and the moral imperative that forces the crew to choose between fleeing (self-preservation) or returning (self-sacrifice).
chain.caused_by_previous: Sets the chain moving by establishing the high-stakes loss of the mentor figure, removing the 'easy' exit and forcing a decision on the survivors.

chain.why_in_plot: Establishes the urgency and the 'certain death' aspect of the rescue mission. Morpheus is being broken by Agents, meaning any rescue is a race against time and likely fatal for the rescuers.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Morpheus's capture in ev-025; his current state of being interrogated and near-breaking defines the stakes of the choice Neo must make.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the core decision point of the plot. Neo explicitly rejects the 'safety' of the prophecy/destiny (which would guarantee his survival) and chooses to risk his life for Morpheus, admitting he is not the One. This transforms the mission from a destiny-fulfillment into a gamble on human loyalty.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the knowledge of Morpheus's imminent breaking (ev-031) and the crew's survival in the previous escape; Neo refuses to let Morpheus die to save himself.

chain.why_in_plot: The physical manifestation of the self-sacrifice choice. The crew enters a 'suicide mission' scenario, risking their lives against overwhelming odds to save another.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Neo's decision in ev-032 to return to the Matrix despite the danger.

chain.why_in_plot: The climax of the rescue attempt. Neo risks his life again to catch Morpheus, demonstrating that his commitment to saving others overrides his own safety even when the plan goes wrong.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the assault in ev-033 reaching its conclusion; the extraction of Morpheus requires Neo to physically intervene to prevent Morpheus's death.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's ultimate test of self-sacrifice. He stands and fights Smith to cover the escape, accepting death as the cost of saving his friends. This is the 'death' part of the 'death and resurrection' arc mentioned in the summary.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the successful rescue in ev-034 and the subsequent pursuit; Neo chooses to stay behind and fight Smith to allow Morpheus and Trinity to escape, sacrificing his own survival.

chain.why_in_plot: The resolution of the dilemma. Neo's self-sacrifice (death) is rewarded with resurrection, validating the choice of sacrifice over self-preservation. Trinity's act of love (another form of risk/sacrifice) also contributes to this outcome.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Neo's death in ev-039; the 'miracle' is the direct consequence of the narrative arc where sacrifice is proven to be the path to transcendence.

definition.name: The Betrayal
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Meaning vs. pleasure — A life of purposeful struggle or empty satisfaction?
definition.summary: Cypher, disillusioned by the 'body count' of the resistance and craving sensory pleasure, bargains with Agent Smith to be re-plugged into the Matrix. He embodies the choice of empty satisfaction over purposeful struggle, murdering his crewmates to secure his own comfortable illusion. His betrayal directly causes Morpheus’s capture, forcing Neo to choose between fleeing the danger Cypher created or engaging in the meaningful, dangerous struggle Cypher fled.

chain.why_in_plot: This event establishes the causal root of the plot: Cypher's disillusionment with the 'body count' of the resistance and his craving for sensory pleasure. It explicitly shows him rejecting purposeful struggle in favor of empty satisfaction by striking a deal with Agent Smith.
chain.caused_by_previous: The chain is set in motion by the cumulative weight of the resistance's failures and the harsh reality of the real world, which Cypher interprets as a 'body count' rather than a meaningful fight, leading him to seek an exit through pleasure.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher actively advances his betrayal by covertly connecting a phone to the Matrix during the mission, enabling the Agents to track the crew. This action directly serves his deal with Smith to secure his own comfortable illusion.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by the bargain struck in ev-020, Cypher now has the motivation and the means (the secret channel to Smith) to sabotage the mission from within.

chain.why_in_plot: The trap springs, resulting in the death of Mouse and the isolation of the crew. This is the direct consequence of Cypher's tracking, forcing the crew into a desperate situation that aligns with Smith's goal of capturing Morpheus.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Cypher's covert phone connection in ev-021, which allowed the Agents to rewrite the Matrix environment around the crew and seal them in the Hotel Lafayette.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus sacrifices himself to save Neo and Trinity. This is the critical turning point where the 'purposeful struggle' is tested, but the capture of Morpheus is the ultimate victory for Cypher's deal, as Smith's primary target is secured.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by the trap in ev-023, which forced the crew into a corner, making Morpheus's sacrifice the only option to save the others, thereby fulfilling the condition of Cypher's deal (delivering Morpheus).

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus is captured. This event confirms the success of Cypher's betrayal and the Agents' operation. It creates the vacuum of leadership and the specific crisis that will force Neo's next choice.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Morpheus's surrender in ev-025, which was the direct result of the trap set by Cypher's betrayal.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher murders his crewmates (Apoc, Switch, and attempts to kill Tank) to secure his re-plugging. This is the physical embodiment of 'empty satisfaction over purposeful struggle,' as he kills his friends to return to a life of sensory pleasure.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by the successful capture of Morpheus in ev-026 and the subsequent regrouping in ev-027, which left Cypher as the only one on the ship with the opportunity to execute the final part of his deal.

chain.why_in_plot: The Agents take Morpheus into custody and begin breaking him. This solidifies the consequence of the betrayal: the leader of the resistance is now in the hands of the system, threatening the entire cause.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the successful delivery of Morpheus in ev-026 and the elimination of the rescue team's immediate threat by Cypher's murders in ev-029.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo chooses to rescue Morpheus. This is the direct counter-stance to Cypher's choice. While Cypher fled to pleasure, Neo chooses the 'meaningful, dangerous struggle' to save his mentor, rejecting the logic of self-preservation and empty satisfaction.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the crisis created by Cypher's betrayal (Morpheus's capture in ev-031 and the crew's decimation in ev-029), which forces Neo to act to preserve the meaning of the resistance.

definition.name: The Choice
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Freedom vs. determinism (fate) — Do we choose, or is the path already written?
definition.summary: The prophecy of the One and the Oracle’s verdict suggest a pre-scripted destiny, yet Neo consistently acts against the expected script, such as refusing to run from Smith in the subway. His refusal to accept the fate Smith pronounces at the point of death serves as the story’s loudest claim that choice overrides destiny. By choosing to stand and fight despite the prophecy of his death, Neo breaks the deterministic cycle and awakens his true power.

chain.why_in_plot: Establishes the deterministic framework (the Prophecy) and the specific stakes (Neo's potential death) that the plot seeks to refute. It sets the 'script' against which Neo will later rebel.
chain.caused_by_previous: Sets the chain moving by introducing the Oracle's verdict and Morpheus's belief in destiny, creating the 'fate' that Neo must eventually break.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo receives the direct, personal prophecy of his death. This is the specific 'written path' he is told to follow, creating the deterministic trap the plot addresses.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows the crew's mission to reach the Oracle (ev-021), which was driven by the need to confirm the prophecy introduced in ev-014.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo explicitly denies being the One, rejecting the deterministic label. His decision to rescue Morpheus is framed as a choice based on belief in a man, not fate, initiating the break from the script.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's capture (ev-025/026) creates the crisis; Neo's refusal to accept the 'One' destiny (ev-022/032 context) allows him to act on personal loyalty rather than prophetic obligation.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo is isolated and trapped, facing the physical manifestation of his fate (Smith). This sets the stage for the final confrontation with determinism.
chain.caused_by_previous: The rescue mission (ev-033/034) and subsequent escape (ev-036) lead to the separation of the crew, leaving Neo alone with Smith.

chain.why_in_plot: The pivotal moment of choice. Neo refuses to run (the expected survival script) and chooses to stand and fight. This is the direct rejection of the 'fate' of death or flight.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's isolation (ev-037) forces the binary choice: run or fight. He chooses to fight, defying the instinct for self-preservation and the prophecy of his death.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo actively rejects Smith's pronouncement of his death ('It's done'). By surviving the 'inevitable' death, he breaks the deterministic cycle and awakens his power, proving choice overrides fate.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's decision to stand (ev-038) leads directly to the battle where Smith attempts to enforce the prophecy of Neo's death, which Neo then defies.

chain.why_in_plot: The culmination of the theme. Neo's awakening is a result of his choice to defy death, not a pre-ordained moment. He destroys the Agent (the enforcer of order/fate) through will, confirming the triumph of choice.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's survival and power surge (ev-039) allow him to return and confront the Agents with new agency, leading to the destruction of Smith.
